main_concerns.concern: The audit-mode tester/reviewer path risks becoming a soft bypass around the developer-readiness gate. If Loom records any downstream role-run artifact after exhaustion, future scripts or humans may read it as 'the pipeline progressed,' even if it does not literally mark E2E passed. The plan is still a narrative until concrete invariants and tests exist.

The audit-mode tester/reviewer path (fix #2) introduces a side-channel that could accidentally mark E2E as passed if any downstream gate misinterprets tester/reviewer output as completion evidence. The plan describes it as producing diagnostic records 'without marking E2E passed,' but provides no guardrail mechanism — no sentinel value, no separate evidence bucket, no flag that downstream gates must check. Without explicit quarantine logic, any future role that consumes tester/reviewer output will see valid-looking evidence and may treat it as sufficient. This is a gate-weakening risk, not a gate-preserving one.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Implement the fixes behind verifiable tests: repeated repair sessions record the correct session id; developer exhaustion launches audit-mode reviewer only and never sets E2E passed; package Prism timeout produces a clear child-probe diagnostic; relation probe selects a domain activity title. Re-review on test output, not on the plan.

Before implementation, add a sentinel field (e.g., `audit_only: true`) to the Loom evidence schema for tester/reviewer output produced after developer exhaustion. Require all downstream gates to check this field and treat audit-only evidence as insufficient for E2E pass. Document this contract in the role protocol so future role authors cannot accidentally consume audit evidence as completion evidence. Additionally, add a smoke test that verifies: when developer exhausts repairs, tester/reviewer runs and produces output, but the final E2E status remains FAILED.
